title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Does parse_deposit_requests enforce two-layer deposit event filtering?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ProcessDepositLog calls contracts.UnpackDepositLogData which uses Ethereum ABI decoder. ABI decoding validates data length and offsets. The deposit event has fixed-size fields (pubkey=48, credentials=32, amount=8, signature=96, index=32).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample. ABI decoder rejects malformed log data. All deposit fields have fixed sizes enforced by the ABI specification.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Reachable only via Ethereum execution layer events (block log scanning), not direct P2P manipulation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: ABI decoding invariant holds: fixed-size fields validated by ABI decoder. ProcessDepositLog returns error on malformed data.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Ethereum ABI decoder + fixed-size field constraints

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: ABI decoder enforces fixed sizes. Not directly attacker-controllable from P2P.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-017: Is compute_requests_hash deterministic across all clients?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: notifyNewPayload passes ExecutionRequests to the execution engine. RequestsHash computation is done by the EL. Prysm verifies the hash received from EL matches the block body's requests hash.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample. Hash computation is handled by the EL; Prysm only validates consistency. SHA256-based requests hash is deterministic.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Only reachable via trusted local execution engine connection.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Requests hash determinism invariant holds: SHA256 is deterministic. EL computes, Prysm validates consistency.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Execution engine is a trusted local component. Hash computation is deterministic.
